title: The Golf Course
victoryHeadline: Caught! Straight down the middle of the truth.
acts:
The Bunkerdown Invitational was less a golf tournament than an annual referendum on the club captain, who had opened the morning with a brand-new 'gimme' rule that, by sheer coincidence, applied to no putt he had ever once needed himself. The field scattered across eight holes still muttering about it before the starter's horn had properly finished.

On Hole 1, Flor idled the cart with one foot riding the pedal, revving gently at the group ahead after swearing that morning she wouldn't let anyone's slow play spoil her tee time — only to discover that absolutely everyone's play was slow. Harry ducked behind the nearest tree the moment he spotted a clipboard coming up the fairway, owing the pro shop nine pounds for a window he'd put a ball through the previous Tuesday and not yet found the nerve to settle. Further along, Iris quietly toed her ball two inches out of a divot and dared her playing partners, with a single look, to say a word about it.

Over on Hole 2, Carson took his fourth run at the same bunker shot, somehow making it worse with each new club he tried, while Gerald — the only man who'd managed to claim the tee that morning — sent his drive almost straight up into the sky and had to be talked out of counting the near miss as a personal best.

On Hole 3, Kent had appointed himself chair of a rules dispute nobody had actually asked him to referee, Mona was holding the flag hostage until the verdict went her way, and Oscar paced the green's top edge heel-to-toe, murmuring distances to nobody in particular. None of the three could have told you, by the end, what the original rule even covered.

On Hole 6, Edna kept one hand steady on the pin and talked Jana, braids tucked behind her ears, through the water carry that had wrecked her card four years running, both of them far too focused on the tee shot to notice much of anything beyond the flag.

Down on Hole 8, Drew stood sentry by the flag, refusing to release it until everyone still on the green had holed out properly, while beside him Lars — having driven the cart directly into the bunker rather than around it — was eleven swings into excavating himself from a wall of sand nearly as tall as he was, certain the twelfth would finally clear the lip.

Up on Hole 4, it was quieter than anywhere else on the course. Club captain Vinny Prewitt stood over his scorecard, filling it in before he'd even finished the hole, while nearby, among a stand of young trees, Berta drifted from sapling to sapling, taking each one by the top in turn and testing, out of an old gardener's habit, exactly how far back it would bend before springing free.

Then came a short, sharp crack and — depending on who you ask — a sound very like a boing. Lars, mid-swing in the bunker, was certain it was Drew finally losing patience with the flag, and didn't look up. Drew was equally certain it was Lars's twelfth attempt going even more wrong than the first eleven, and didn't look up either. It took a second, more insistent shout from the marshal's cart, and the better part of six unhurried minutes, before anyone walked the length of the course to Hole 4, where Vinny's scorecard lay half-filled in the grass, his pencil still in hand, and nothing nearby to explain any of it.

whereabouts.A: Anna spent a good forty minutes at the Hole 5 waterline scooping her own ball back out of the drink with a telescoping net, insisting each time that this one would be the last she ever lost there.
whereabouts.B: Berta stood among the young trees on Hole 4, keeping Vinny loose company while he filled in his card, and doing what she always did around a sapling — taking it by the top and testing, out of old gardening habit, exactly how far back it would spring.
whereabouts.C: Carson took his fourth run at the same bunker shot on Hole 2, certain the fifth would finally be the one, and increasingly unable to explain to Gerald why he kept switching clubs instead of his technique.
whereabouts.D: Drew planted himself by the flag on Hole 8 in his flat cap, refusing to pull the pin for anyone until they'd holed out properly, a rule he had invented himself and enforced with total sincerity.
whereabouts.E: Edna stood by the flag on Hole 6, one hand steady on the pin, quietly coaching Jana through the tee shot that had beaten her four years running, and hoping, more than she'd ever admit, that this might finally be the year.
whereabouts.F: Flor idled the cart on Hole 1 with one foot on the pedal, revving gently at the group ahead, having sworn that morning she wouldn't let anyone's slow play ruin her tee time and then discovering that absolutely everyone's play was slow.
whereabouts.G: Gerald, the only man who'd managed to claim the tee that morning, sent his drive on Hole 2 almost straight up into the sky, watched it come down roughly where he was standing, and had to be talked out of counting the near miss as a personal best.
whereabouts.H: Harry ducked behind a tree on Hole 1 the moment he spotted the pro-shop assistant walking the fairway with a clipboard, owing the club nine pounds for a window he'd put a ball through the previous Tuesday and not yet found the nerve to settle.
whereabouts.I: Iris, up the fairway on Hole 1, nudged her ball two inches out of a divot with the toe of her shoe and dared her playing partners, with a single look, to say a word about it.
whereabouts.J: Jana stood on the Hole 6 tee lining up the water carry that had wrecked her card four years running, braids tucked behind her ears, telling herself out loud that this year was different.
whereabouts.K: Kent, on Hole 3, appointed himself chair of a rules dispute nobody had actually asked him to settle, and was already losing the argument to two people with considerably less confidence than him.
whereabouts.L: Lars had driven the cart straight into the Hole 8 bunker rather than around it, and was now eleven swings into excavating a wall of sand nearly as tall as he was, glasses fogged, insisting the twelfth would clear it.
whereabouts.M: Mona took possession of the flag on Hole 3 and refused to hand it back until the argument beside her reached a verdict she personally agreed with.
whereabouts.N: Naomi hadn't left the sand pit on Hole 7 in over an hour, sunglasses on, a paperback tucked behind her golf bag, having quietly worked out that nobody bothers you in a bunker.
whereabouts.O: Oscar paced the top edge of Hole 3 heel-to-toe, murmuring distances under his breath — a habit left over from a surveying course he'd taken on a whim two winters ago and never mentioned to a single person at the club.
whereabouts.V: Vinny stood on Hole 4 filling in his scorecard before he'd even finished the hole, already rehearsing how he'd explain his new gimme rule to whichever committee member complained about it first.

reveal: It was Berta, on Hole 4, and the tree did the work. While Vinny stood reciting his gimme rule to an audience that had stopped listening, Berta finished testing her sapling one time too many — pulling it flat to the turf, hooking the strap of his golf bag over the bent trunk, and letting go. Fourteen clubs and a full thermos went up and over in one violent arc, and Vinny went down with them, pencil still in his hand and the new rule still half out of his mouth. Berta straightened her cardigan, murmured an apology to a tree that had done nothing wrong, and went to find her own ball, which — she noted with quiet satisfaction — had landed in an excellent lie.

escape.generic: The club filed it under 'unusual course conditions', Vinny's gimme rule was quietly repealed by unanimous and unrecorded vote, and the real killer finished the back nine in a very good mood.

byAccused.A: Anna's telescoping net stayed propped against the Hole 5 lost-and-found box for a week before anyone thought to return it, by which point three more balls had gone into the water uncontested.
byAccused.C: "I only ever changed clubs because the last one wasn't working," Carson kept saying, to steadily diminishing sympathy, all the way to the clubhouse.
byAccused.D: Drew was hauled off Hole 8 still holding the flag, insisting — accurately, as it turned out — that he had never once left his post all afternoon.
byAccused.E: Jana finished the water carry alone five minutes after Edna was led away, cleared it clean for the first time in four years, and had nobody left on the tee to tell.
byAccused.F: Flor was pulled out of the cart still revving gently at the group ahead of her, who by then had a considerably better excuse for holding everyone up than she ever had.
byAccused.G: The club quietly credited Gerald's runaway tee shot with knocking a nest out of a tree three fairways over, which nobody could prove and everybody, deep down, believed.
byAccused.H: Harry's nine pounds sat paid and forgotten in the pro shop till, the one entirely clean item in his whole afternoon, which did him no good at all once the cuffs came out anyway.
byAccused.I: "It was already a bad lie," Iris told the marshals, entirely truthfully, about a completely different offence than the one they were asking about.
byAccused.J: The clubhouse noticeboard credited Jana's finally-clean water carry to 'improved conditions', and nobody ever got round to telling her it was really just Edna's coaching, since Edna wasn't there to take the credit.
byAccused.K: Kent was marched off Hole 3 still chairing a dispute that dissolved, mid-sentence, the moment he was gone.
byAccused.L: Lars was pulled bodily out of the Hole 8 bunker on his twelfth swing, sand still in his beard, and never did find out whether it would have finally cleared the lip.
byAccused.M: The flag on Hole 3 stood ownerless for the rest of the afternoon, since Mona had been the only one willing to hold it, and the rules dispute it was hostage to went unresolved forever.
byAccused.N: Naomi's paperback was found face-down and open in the Hole 7 bunker days later, and whoever found it never did learn how the story ended, which felt, on reflection, like roughly the right amount of justice.
byAccused.O: Oscar's surveying notebook turned up in the investigation marked 'evidence', which is how the whole club finally learned about the course he'd taken two winters ago — a smaller scandal that briefly eclipsed the arrest itself.
